title: The multitude falls
summary: After King Benjamin finishes speaking, he looks around and sees the multitude fallen to the earth in fear of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin finishes speaking the words delivered to him by the angel of the Lord.
He looks around at the multitude, who have fallen to the earth because fear of the Lord has come upon them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin is positioned where he can see the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, clothing, architecture, and appearance of the multitude.

narration.text: they had fallen to the earth

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the angel as present; the verse only refers to words previously delivered by the angel.

title: The multitude cries for mercy
summary: The multitude recognizes its fallen state and cries aloud together for mercy and forgiveness.

explicit_facts.text: The people see themselves in their carnal state, less than the dust of the earth, and cry aloud with one voice.
They ask for mercy, forgiveness, purified hearts, and affirm belief in Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude remains fallen to the earth as it cries.
unspecified_visual_details: The size and arrangement of the multitude and their individual expressions.

spoken_dialogue.text: O have mercy, and apply the atoning blood of Christ that we may receive forgiveness of our sins, and our hearts may be purified;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the multitude

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Their statement that Christ shall come among the children of men is belief expressed by the multitude, not a present visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ or an atoning event in this scene.

title: Joy and peace
summary: After they speak, the Spirit of the Lord comes upon them. They receive a remission of their sins and are filled with joy and peace of conscience.

explicit_facts.text: After they had spoken, the Spirit of the Lord came upon them.
They were filled with joy, received a remission of their sins, and had peace of conscience.
Their peace of conscience followed their exceeding faith in Jesus Christ, who should come according to King Benjamin's words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown expressing joy.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible appearance of the Spirit of the Lord.

narration.text: and they were filled with joy, having received a remission of their sins, and having peace of conscience,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes no visible form for the Spirit of the Lord.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible manifestation, light, or figure for the Spirit of the Lord.
Do not invent the words the people spoke.

title: Benjamin resumes speaking
summary: King Benjamin addresses the people again and calls their attention to the remainder of his words.

explicit_facts.text: King Benjamin opens his mouth and begins speaking to the people, asking them to hear and understand the remainder of his words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin addresses the gathered multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: His precise position, gestures, and surroundings.

spoken_dialogue.text: My friends and my brethren, my kindred and my people, I would again call your attention, that ye may hear and understand the remainder of my words which I shall speak unto you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

title: Knowledge of God's goodness
summary: King Benjamin teaches about recognizing human frailty and knowing God's goodness, power, wisdom, patience, and long-suffering.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin teaches that knowledge of God's goodness can awaken people to a sense of their nothingness and fallen state.
He speaks of God's power, wisdom, patience, and long-suffering toward humanity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: King Benjamin's teaching continues as speech over the supported setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any symbolic imagery or specific appearance of God.

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, if the knowledge of the goodness of God at this time has awakened you to a sense of your nothingness, and your worthless and fallen state—
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: I say unto you, if ye have come to a knowledge of the goodness of God, and his matchless power, and his wisdom, and his patience, and his long-suffering towards the children of men;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The description of human nothingness is figurative teaching, not a literal visual transformation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict people physically shrinking or becoming dust.

title: Salvation through the atonement
summary: Benjamin teaches that salvation comes through the atonement for those who trust in the Lord, keep the commandments, and continue in faith.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin teaches that the atonement was prepared from the foundation of the world so salvation might come to those who trust in the Lord, keep his commandments, and continue in faith to the end of mortal life.
He says salvation through the atonement is for all mankind, past, present, and future.
He says there is no other salvation or condition by which people can be saved than what he has described.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin speaks to his listeners from the same unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal visual representation of the atonement or salvation.

spoken_dialogue.text: And this is the means whereby salvation cometh.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The atonement and salvation are teachings here, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a separate atonement scene or supernatural event.

title: Believe and repent
summary: Benjamin urges the people to believe in God, repent, humble themselves, ask forgiveness sincerely, and act on their beliefs.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin tells the people to believe God exists, created all things, has all wisdom and power, and comprehends what humans do not.
He tells them to repent, forsake sins, humble themselves, sincerely ask forgiveness, and do these things if they believe.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin's teaching is delivered as off-screen speech over the established setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any depiction of God or creation.

spoken_dialogue.text: Believe in God; believe that he is, and that he created all things, both in heaven and in earth;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: And again, believe that ye must repent of your sins and forsake them, and humble yourselves before God;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Creation and God's comprehension are teachings, not a narrated visual scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show God appearing or stage a visual creation sequence.

title: Remember and remain steadfast
summary: Benjamin asks the people to remember God's greatness and goodness, remain humble and faithful, and says they will rejoice and retain remission of sins.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin urges remembrance of God's greatness, human nothingness, God's goodness and long-suffering, humility, daily prayer, and steadfast faith in what the angel spoke of.
He says those who do this will rejoice, be filled with God's love, retain remission of sins, and grow in knowledge of what is just and true.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin continues teaching from the established setting.
unspecified_visual_details: A visible form for God's love, remission of sins, or future events.

spoken_dialogue.text: And behold, I say unto you that if ye do this ye shall always rejoice, and be filled with the love of God,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The promised outcomes are teachings, not additional present-tense events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the angel or a visible embodiment of God's love.

title: Peaceful living and care for children
summary: Benjamin teaches against injuring one another and instructs parents to provide for, guide, and teach their children to love and serve.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin says the people will not intend to injure one another, but will live peaceably and render to each person what is due.
He says they will not allow their children to go hungry or naked, transgress God's laws, fight, or quarrel.
He says they will teach their children truth, soberness, love, and service to one another.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be shown over the established setting without staging the conditional examples as current events.
unspecified_visual_details: The children and family settings described only as future instruction.

spoken_dialogue.text: But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses describe expected conduct, not a narrated family scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent visible children or a quarrel as a present event.

title: Succor those in need
summary: Benjamin urges people to give substance to those in need and warns against withholding help on the grounds that a person's misery is deserved.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin tells the people to succor those in need, give substance, and not turn away a beggar to perish.
He presents the possible excuse that a man brought misery on himself and should receive no food or aid.
He says a person who does this has cause to repent and, unless he repents, perishes and has no interest in God's kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin's words can be presented as off-screen speech over the established setting.
unspecified_visual_details: A specific beggar or place of giving, neither narrated as present.

spoken_dialogue.text: And also, ye yourselves will succor those that stand in need of your succor;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: Perhaps thou shalt say: The man has brought upon himself his misery;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The hypothetical excuse and warning are teachings, not a narrated encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a specific person refusing a beggar.

title: All depend on God
summary: Benjamin reminds the people that everyone depends on God and recalls that God answered their plea for remission by pouring out his Spirit and filling their hearts with joy.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin asks whether all are beggars, dependent on God for food, clothing, and all riches.
He recalls that the people called on God for remission of sins, and God poured out his Spirit and filled their hearts with joy.
He urges them, because they depend on God, to impart their substance to one another.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin speaks to the multitude; the reference to their earlier prayer is recalled speech about an earlier event.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible form for God or the Spirit.

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, are we not all beggars?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: Nay;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: O then, how ye ought to impart of the substance that ye have one to another.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 20 recalls the people's earlier experience; do not turn that report into a new present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a new divine appearance or repeat the earlier prayer as occurring now.

title: Warning to those who withhold
summary: Benjamin warns that condemning a petitioner while withholding one's substance brings condemnation, addressing those rich in worldly things.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin says those who condemn a petitioner and withhold substance are condemning themselves, since life and substance belong to God.
He pronounces woe on such a man and directs these words to those rich in worldly things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning is delivered as speech over the established setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Any particular rich person, petitioner, or transfer of goods.

spoken_dialogue.text: I say unto you, wo be unto that man,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warning is conditional teaching, not an account of a specific refusal.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible rich listener or petitioner.

title: The poor and the would-be giver
summary: Benjamin addresses people who have little but enough to get by, saying they remain guiltless if they would give were they able.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin addresses the poor who have sufficient to remain from day to day, including those who deny a beggar because they lack means.
He says they remain guiltless if they sincerely would give if they had means; otherwise they are condemned for coveting what they have not received.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin speaks to the gathered listeners without staging a particular exchange.
unspecified_visual_details: The material circumstances or appearance of any poor person.

spoken_dialogue.text: I give not because I have not, but if I had I would give.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The words are a hypothetical statement of the heart, not a reported spoken reply from a named person.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the quoted hypothetical as speech by an invented visible individual.

title: Give according to what one has
summary: Benjamin calls for giving to the poor through practical care, and says these actions should be done diligently, in wisdom, and in order.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin urges people to impart substance to the poor according to what each has, feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, and visiting and relieving the sick.
He says to do these things in wisdom and order, not running faster than one's strength, and to be diligent.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The practical examples can be conveyed through Benjamin's speech without depicting separate acts as current events.
unspecified_visual_details: The people who might receive aid and the places where aid might be given.

spoken_dialogue.text: I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are instructions and examples, not a sequence of narrated acts.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage distinct feeding, clothing, or sick-visiting events.

title: Return what you borrow
summary: Benjamin instructs borrowers to return what they borrow as agreed and notes that there are many ways to sin.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin says a borrower should return the borrowed thing according to agreement, or commit sin and perhaps cause the neighbor to sin.
He says he cannot enumerate all the many ways and means by which a person may commit sin.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin continues his address to the listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: Any particular borrower, neighbor, loan, or object.

spoken_dialogue.text: And I would that ye should remember, that whosoever among you borroweth of his neighbor should return the thing that he borroweth,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

spoken_dialogue.text: And finally, I cannot tell you all the things whereby ye may commit sin;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The borrowing example is instruction, not a narrated transaction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a borrower, lender, or object.

title: Watch yourselves to the end
summary: Benjamin concludes by warning the people to watch their thoughts, words, and deeds, keep God's commandments, and continue in faith.

explicit_facts.text: Benjamin warns the people to watch themselves, their thoughts, words, and deeds, observe God's commandments, and continue in faith to the end of their lives.
He tells the people to remember and not perish.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Benjamin delivers the concluding warning to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience's reactions and the physical setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now, O man, remember, and perish not.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Benjamin
